newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ranariddh loyalists in hiding - sources.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh loyalists in hiding - sources.

text.p: Several leading officials of Cambodia's ousted First Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh are in hiding after the arrest by strongman Hun Sen's forces and execution of a senior Ranariddh loyalist, officials of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party said on Wednesday.
"We are safe for now ... we are in a hotel," one nervous FUNCINPEC official told Reuters on Wednesday morning, referring to himself and his family.
Hun Sen's troops arrested interior ministry secretary of state Ho Sok on Monday and he was later shot dead, an interior ministry official told reporters on Tuesday.
Khieu Sopheak, an interior ministry adviser loyal to Hun Sen, said Ho Sok had been involved in "sabotage and plots".
"He was shot down by the people that were angry with him," he told reporters. He did not say when Ho Sok was killed or exactly who had killed him.
The fate of a further senior member of Ranariddh's party, Chao Sambath, was unclear on Wednesday.
An Interior Ministry official loyal to Hun Sen said Chao Sambath, a senior intelligence officer in Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party had been arrested.
Other senior officials under Hun Sen could not immediately confirm the arrest and one said Chao Sambath was expected to be picked up by Hun Sen's forces very soon.

FUNCINPEC sources said while some party members were hiding in the capital, others were trying to leave the country in the aftermath of two days of fighting in the city and Hun Sen's ousting of Ranariddh on Sunday. Ranariddh is presently in France.
Chao Sambath and Ho Sok were among four senior FUNCINPEC members identified by Hun Sen as being responsible for the two days of fighting in the capital at the weekend.
The weekend of violence claimed at least 58 lives and hundreds of foreigners have since fled the country.
Hun Sen said the four had to be hunted down and arrested.
The other two senior FUNCINPEC loyalists identified by Hun Sen were Ranariddh's top military man General Nhiek Bun Chaay and FUNCINPEC security official Serey Kosal.

Nhiek Bun Chaay fled Phnom Penh on Sunday night with his troops as Hun Sen's forces took control of the capital and its outskirts after two days of fighting. His whereabouts were not immediately known.
One Interior Ministry official said on Tuesday Hun Sen's forces were closing in on the general in an area some 30 km (20 miles) north of the capital.
